brief: TME's September 23 call argued Nvidia didn't need to lose existing orders for the AAPL/NVDA relative narrative to shift, reasoning that AI inference moving onto devices and local machines could cap Nvidia's share of incremental AI demand. At the time Goldman had flagged NVDA implied volatility at its lowest since before COVID while the stock traded near range highs, so TME's preferred trade was long AAPL calls versus long NVDA puts, on the view that an inference-narrative shift could hit NVDA before earnings estimates moved. That trade delivered as the AAPL/NVDA gap exploded, accelerated by recent Huang news, and TME now says to close it. Separately, at today's lows NVDA was down nearly 40% from its early-October highs and nearly 30% below its 200-day moving average, matching extremes from the earlier Liberation Day drawdown, which exceeded 40% but unfolded more slowly. Goldman's Jim Schneider parallels this to Apple's 2011 multiple compression after Steve Jobs' departure (forward P/E 17x to 12x, bottoming near 9x in 2013, then recovering), expecting similar uncertainty for Nvidia until leadership and momentum clarify, but sees attractive risk/reward given Goldman's roughly 80% EPS growth forecast.
